data.narrative:
Planet Labs is a public-stage Space & Aerospace company that has raised over $700M and currently trades at $7.56B. The valuation analysis draws from a peer universe of 3 same-sector, same-stage public companies: Rocket Lab ($40.0B), Firefly Aerospace ($2.9B), and Astroscale ($840M), with a broader comp set including 5 additional public tickers and 8 private peers.

The peer-median method is the applicable triangulation approach here. Across the three stage-matched public comparables, the median valuation is $2.9B, with a range spanning $840M to $40.0B. This wide dispersion reflects material heterogeneity in the Space & Aerospace public market. A public P/S multiple approach—using the sector median of 25.3x across six tickers—cannot be applied without disclosure of Planet Labs' revenue, which private companies typically withhold.

The triangulated range supports a valuation of $2.5B to $3.3B (median $2.9B), substantially below the current public market price of $7.56B. The primary uncertainty is whether Planet Labs' market position, growth rate, or technical differentiation justify a premium to the peer median. The wide dispersion in comparable valuations ($840M–$40.0B) also signals that single-method peer analysis in this sector carries considerable model risk. Additional visibility into revenue, unit economics, and customer concentration would sharpen valuation confidence.
